Definition: from G3326 and G142; to betake oneself, i.e. remove (locally):--depart.
BiblicalUsage: Matthew uses this word at the seams of Jesus' teaching, when He finished one set of parables and departed, and again when He finished His sayings in Galilee and went toward Judea. It is the ordinary word for moving on after the teaching is done.
TheologicalSignificance: I notice that Jesus never lingered where His word had been given: He taught, and then He departed, and the teaching went with Him to the next place that needed it.
